title: Generation flow for AI professional headshots
prompt: Users upload photos to generate professional headshots. High-quality output needs many seconds-to-minutes of GPU per image. How should you structure the generation flow so users get their result?
constraint: High-quality results take many seconds-to-minutes of GPU; users will wait for quality but want feedback that something is happening.

options.why: Directly serves the constraint: the cheap preview gives the immediate feedback users want (they see their face, style, framing in seconds), while the multi-minute high-quality render runs async and notifies on completion. Users get quality AND responsiveness without holding a connection open for minutes.

Defensible — async correctly avoids blocking on minutes of GPU, and the constraint confirms users will wait for quality. But with no preview the user stares at a spinner or empty screen, missing the 'want feedback' half of the constraint; weaker than pairing it with an instant preview.

Fails the constraint: holding an HTTP/connection open for many seconds-to-minutes of GPU work ties up resources, risks timeouts, and gives the user zero feedback while they wait. The workload is explicitly too slow for a real-time blocking path.

Violates the constraint's core premise: users will wait for quality, so trading away the high-quality result to hit real-time latency sacrifices the exact thing they came for. Speed here is not the priority — feedback during a justified wait is.
